thread.title: It’s the End of the World! Nasdaq Breaks 7000, Dow Gains 100 Points as 2018 Starts With a Bang

author: Ben Levisohn
title: It’s the End of the World! Nasdaq Breaks 7000, Dow Gains 100 Points as 2018 Starts With a Bang
text:
It was a happy New Year for investors as the Nasdaq rallied above 7,000 for the first time and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained more than 100 points.
Illustration: Getty Images The S&P 500 rose 0.8% to 2695.79, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 104.79 points, or 0.4%, to 24,824.01. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.5% to 7006.90, its first close above 7000. Even small caps surged as the Russell 2000 climbed 0.9% to 1,550.01. Both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq closed at new all-time highs, though the Nasdaq remains below its inflation-adjusted high of 7,275.
Now some will make a lot of noise about the fact that Nasdaq soared over 7000, covering the ground from 6000 in just 174 days, and maybe even compare it to the dot-com bubble. Oh wait, they did: The Wall Street Journal described it as " a pace not seen since the heights of the technology boom ." But let's do a little math here. The Nasdaq gained 17% to get from 6000 to 7000, an average of 0.1 point day. That's pretty fast. But in 1998, the Nasdaq took just 38 days to go from 3000 to 4000. That's a 33% rise, which averages out to 0.85 point a day. And from 4000 to 5000, a 20% rise, took just 49 days, or 0.51 point a day. The rallies from 3000 to 4000, and then 4000 to 5000 were signs of a bubble (but even then, a lousy timing mechanism). The current one is just the sign of a very strong market.
Which doesn't mean it doesn't come with risks (you don't end a bubble for a bull market to top). Today's market was driven higher by big tech, including the FANGs-- Facebook ( FB ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ), and Alphabet ( GOOGL ), the company once known as Google- -as well as the biggest of the big, Apple ( AAPL ). And with the hot staying hot, the biggest challenge facing portfolio managers in 2018 might be outperforming the market, says Satya Pradhuman , research director at Cirrus Research . See, Pradhuman contends that market leadership will narrow in 2018, as more of the gains become focused in fewer stocks. This forces managers to make a choice, he says. "Investors will suffer the angst of knowing that they are traveling further out on the risk curve to simply match benchmark returns," Pradhuman writes. The other option is underperforming. He dubs it the "Icarus dilemma."
I call it trouble.
